full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This revisional application directed against the judgment and decree dated 11-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka in Title Appeal 623 of 1999 reversing those dated 29-8-1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. 2. The present revision was heard by Single Bench of this court and by judgment and order dated 31-8-2004 made the rule absolute and the judgment and decree dated 11-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka set aside and those of the trial court are restored and suit was decreed. 3. Thereafter opposite parties No. 1 and 2 filed a review application on 13-12-2004 but same was not registered as review application. Subsequently, by the judgment and order dated 7-3-2005 review application was rejected and rule was made absolute and the judgment and decree passed by the court below are set aside and the suit was sent back on remand to the trial court for fresh hearing and further directed to complete the hearing of the case within six months from the date of receipt of the order. 4. Against the judgment and order dated 7-3-2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 6307 of 2001 the plaintiffs-petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 507 of 2007 and after hearing leave was granted on 6-8-2006 giving rise to Civil Appeal No 111 of 2006. The defendant nos. 1 and 2 also filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1632 of 2005 and leave was granted giving rise to Civil Appeal No.102of 2007. Both the Appeal were heard together and the Appellate Division by judgment dated 23-6-2015 set aside the judgment and order of the High Court Division and sent the matter to the High Court Division for hearing of the revision afresh presided over by AKM Abdul Hakim, J and further directed to hear the revision and dispose of the same within 2 months from the date of receipt of this judgment. 5. Before we enter into the merit of the revisional application, let us first deal with the applications filed by the opposite parties for reconstruction of file for the missing Exhibits of the defendants-opposite parties herein which is necessary for proper disposal of this revision on merit. 6. It appears that this matter was appeared in the daily cause list on 7-2-2016, on that date Mr AKM Badrudduza, the learned Advocate filed fresh power on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 with no objection certificate issued by the filing Advocate for the opposite-parties, Mr Shaheed Alam. Sub-sequently, Mr Tushar Kanti Roy, the learned Advocate filed fresh power on behalf of the petitioners on 27-3-2016. 7. At the time of hearing of the revision, it appears that the Lower Court Record is not available. In such circumstances, opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application for calling of the Lower Court Record. Accordingly this court allowed the said application by order dated 8-12-2016 and directed the learned Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat-4, Dhaka and Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka to sent the Lower Court Record of Title Appeal No. 623 of 1999 and Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 within two weeks from the date of receipt of the order. 8. In compliance of the said order, two files LCR of Title Appeal No. 623 of 1999 was sent to this court by memo dated 5-1-2017. After scrutiny of the case record, section reported that except SA Khatian (Exhibit-2) all other Exhibits Nos.1-3 to 14(Ka) are available in the case record, but the record of the Title Suit No. 3 of 1991was not sent to this court. Subsequently, another notice was sent by the office to transmit the record of Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. Thereafter, Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court, Dhaka, by memo dated 9-1-2017 informed that the LCR of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 has been destroyed in the year 2015 as such could not send the Lower Court Record. 9. In such circumstances, when the record has been destroyed defendant No.1 as substituted heir of defendant-opposite party No.2 was compelled to file an application on 14-5-2017 under Section 151 for reconstruction of the file for missing Exhibits of the defendants along with photostate copies of those missing Exhibit Nos. Ka-Cha. The matter was appeared in the daily cause list on 24-8-2017 but the hearing of the application was adjourned till 23-11-2017. Subsequently, on 23-5-2018 petitioners filed supplementary-affidavit by taking some new grounds in the present revisional application. 10. Against the supplementary-affidavit of the petitioners dated 23-5-2018, the defendant-opposite party Nos.1 and 2 filed supplementary-affidavit on 27-5-2018 stating that section 94(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates that in order to prevent the ends of justice from being defeated the court may, if it is so prescribed make such other interlocutory orders as may appear to the court to be just and convenient. Since the petitioner in his supplementary-affidavit dated 23-5-2018 stated that only trial court reconsidered the case record as per Civil Rules and Order. On 16-11-2017 opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed another supplementary-affidavit that stating defendants missing Exhibits were destroyed when the case record was sent from the High Court Division to the trial court. The opposite party No.2 after much effort able to collect certified copies of Exhibit-"Ka-"Ga' and "Uma' and "Cha 'and photocopy of the Exhibit-Ga but failed to submit Exhibit-1' and submitted those Exhibits by list of documents with the supplementary-affidavit, which is described below:

11. It appears that Exhibit-'Ga' is the original registered Sale Deed No. 9400 dated 21-4-1985 executed by Keshob Lal son of late Radhu Mistry and Ahladi Bewa wife of late Ishar Mali of Dhonia, Demra, in favour of Ali Akbor, Samsul Haque son of late Akram Khan of Donia, Police Station-Demra, Dhaka. The certified copy of the said sale deed dated 21-4-1985 was produced by the plaintiffs-petitioners in the trial which was also marked as Exhibit-9. Subsequently, on 26-7-2018 learned Advocate for the petitioner filed photocopy of the original Sale Deed dated 21-4-1985 marked in the Tile Suit No 3 of 1991on 18-7-1999 as (Exhibit-Ga) filed before this court along with the photocopy of SA Khatian (Exhibit-2) which was missing from the LCR and accordingly same was kept with the record. Since both contesting parties agreed that the exhibited documents filed by the defendant-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 on 16-11-2017 are the same document which was marked in the suit as Exhibit No. 2 and `Ga' respectively. The two documents are kabala dated 21-4-1985 (Exhibit-Ga) and SA khatian (Exhibit-2) which was subsequently filed by the plaintiff petitioner before this court on 26-11-2017. Since all this documents were reconstructed by the learned advocate of both the parties and they have no objection for such reconstruction. Accordingly, the missing documents Exhibit Nos. Ka-Cha filed by the defendants and Exhibit-ga and Exhibit-2 is reconstructed. The above reconstructed Exhibited documents be kept with the record under separate list of documents prepared by this court on 21-1-2019 Accordingly the application for reconstruction of missing Exhibited documents filed by the opposite party is allowed. The list of reconstructed Exhibited document prepared by this court on 21-1-2019 kept with the record. 12. Further for proper authenticity of the missing Exhibits, we have collected the paper book from the Appellate Division prepared in Civil Appeal No. 102 of 2007 and Civil Appeal No. 111 of 2006 arising from the judgment and order dated 7-3-2005 passed by the High Court in Civil Revision No. 6307 of 2001. After scrutiny of the Paper Book it appears that the Exhibited documents which are reconstructed in the present revision are same documents filed by the parties in the Appellate Division and included in the Paper Book prepared in the said two Civil Appeals No 102 and 111 of 2006. 13. It may be noted that although the matter was sent from the Appellate Division to hear and dispose of the same within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the judgment. After receipt of Judgment from the Appellate Division the matter was posted in the daily cause list for hearing. As we have already stated that due to the destruction of the exhibited documents of the defendant Nos. I and 2 by the trial court, matter could not be heard for last three and half years. Since record was reconstructed in respect of the exhibited documents of the defendants, which were marked as Exhibit-ka-cha, now we have taken to dispose of this civil revision. 14. The facts, in short, are that the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka on 7-1-1991 declaring that the deed described in the 'Ga' schedule is void and restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by decree of permanent injunction from disturbing possession of the plaintiff in the 'ka' schedule land. The suit was filed seeking declaration of title, confirmation of possession and also for permanent injunction in respect of the land described of the schedule 'ka' and for cancellation of the kabala described in schedule 'ga' to the plaint. 15. The positive case of the plaintiff, is that, the suit land belonged to Ahladi Bewa and CS record was prepared in her name and she died leaving only son Shamboo Nath who died leaving wife Sreemoti Bewa; that Sreemoti Bewa by kabala dated 28-4-1952 sold the land that she got from Shamboo Nath to Khetro Mohan Baroi; that Khetro Mohan Baroi entered into an oral agreement on 14-8-1961 with the plaintiff for selling the land and upon receiving Taka 500 delivered possession to the plaintiff, that prior to the registration of the Kabala Khetro Mohan died leaving two sons, Madhu Sudhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjon Baroi as his heirs and the said two sons upon attaining majority sold on 13-5-1969 the land as to which their father entered into contract to sell to the plaintiff; that SA record was wrongly prepared in the name of Ahladi Bewa and Sadhu Charan and about the said wrong record Khetro Mohan Baroi had knowledge; that plaintiff for correction of the record filed Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 in the Sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for correction of SA and RS Khatian and the same was decreed ex-parte on 27-3-1989 that while plaintiff took steps for correction of the record on the basis of the said decree, it was found that the land in the suit has mutated in the name of the defendant on the basis of the forged kabala; that the plaintiff obtained certified copy of the kabala on 22-9-1990 and on the basis of which defendant claimed the land and filed Mutation Case No. 275 of 1990 before the Assistant Commissioner (land) for correction of the record and in due course plaintiffs got their names mutated by cancelling mutation of defendant Nos. 1 and 2; that the defendant having had suffered defeat in the miscellaneous case threatened the plaintiff on 28-12-1990 to dispossess from the suit land. Hence the suit. 16. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, interalia, that the suit is barred by limitation; not maintainable and also that Ahladi Bewa was the original owner and CS Khatian was prepared in her name and that SA record was also recorded in the name of Ahladi Bewa and Sadhu Charan Mondal; that defendants entered into contract with Ahladi Bewa and Keshob Lal on 1-10-1975 and the said persons executed several deeds of agreement for sale and delivered possession to the defendants upon receiving Taka 18,000 and subsequently on 20-4-1985 they executed Sale Deed and the defendants have been living in the land by making construction. 17. The learned trial court framed 5 issues which are as follows: i) Is the suit is maintainable in its present form? (ii) Is the suit is bad for defect of parties? (iii) Is the suit is barred by limitation? (iv) Have the plaintiff any right title, interest and possession in the disputed land? (v) Are the plaintiffs entitle to get decree as they prayed for? 18. In the suit the plaintiffs have examined 6 witnesses, including plaintiff No.2. On the other hand, defendants in support their case examined 5 witnesses including defendant No.-1. Plaintiffs produced their documents which were marked as Exhibits 1-14 and defendant's documents were marked as Exhibit 'As'-'14'. 19. After contested hearing trial court by the judgment and decree dated 29-8-1999 decreed the suit on the finding that the suit is not barred by limitation, bad for defect of party and the suit as framed is quite maintainable; that the plaintiffs are in possession and have been able to prove their possession in the suit land. Accordingly suit was decreed and declared that the deed described in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint is cancelled and also passed a decree for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from creating any obstacle in peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the 'ka' schedule of land. 20. Defendants went on appeal and the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka by judgment and decree dated 11-10-2001 allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court on the finding that the plaintiff have no right, title, and interest in the suit land and plaintiffs are not entitled to relief as to cancellation of the deed and for a decree of permanent injunction. 21. Against the judgment and decree of the appellate court the plaintiffs filed present civil revision before this court and obtained the present rule. 22. In due course, the said Civil Revision No. 6307 of 2001 rule was heard and disposed of by the Single Bench of this Division by judgment and order dated 31-8-2004 made the rule absolute and the judgment and decree dated 11-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka was set aside and the judgment of the trial court was restored and accordingly the suit was decreed. Against the said order of the High Court opposite party No. 1 and 2 filed a review application dated 13-12-2004 and the said review application was heard by a single Bench of the High Court Division, by judgment and decree dated 7-5-2005 allowed the said application and sent back the case on remand to the trial court after setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the court below. It may be noted that although the High Court Division passed Judgment without registering the same as Review application but passed Judgment in earlier Civil Revision No. 6307 of 2001. 23. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 7-5-2005 plaintiffs-present petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 507 of 2005 and leave was granted giving rise to Civil Appeal No 111of 2006. The defendants-opposite parties also filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No 1632 of 2005 and leave was granted giving rise to Civil Appeal No. 102 of 2007. Both appeals were heard together and the Appellate Division by judgment dated 23-6-2015 set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and sent back the matter to the High Court Division for hearing the revision afresh by this Bench. 24. Mr Tushar Kanti Roy, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal. He further submits that the teamed Appellate Court failed to consider that PW 1 in his deposition stated that Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 was filed for correction of the SA record and got ex-parte decree dated 23-7-1989. But the learned Appellate Court failed to consider that the ex-parte decree was not obtained by fraud or collusively and left it out from consideration. Although the defendants had opportunity to challenge the said judgment by filing an independent suit or challenge the said ex-parte decree in the present suit. He next submits that the learned Appellate Court failed to consider the report submitted by the Chairman Shyampur Union Parishad to the Assistant Commissioner land Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka dated 10-2-1991(Exhibit-7) and certificate of the Chairman Shyampur Union Parishad dated 22-12-1985 (Exhibit-8) and specially Exhibit-5 from which it evident that Ahladi Bewa died long before the independence of Bangladesh and Ahladi Bewa died leaving behind only son Shamboo Nath and Shamboo Nath, who died leaving widow Sreemoti Bewa and PW4 categorically stated that Ahladi Bewa died in the year 1949. He also submits that the plaintiff successfully proved the possession in the suit land by paying rents by Exhibit-11 series. But the lower court failed to find that the plaintiff Md Imam Uddin paid rent in the name of recorded tenant, Ahladi Bewa from 1354 BS to 1363 BS same was paid to the zaminder sheresta whereas zamindar was not entitled to receive rent after 1356 BS. He finally submits that the learned Appellate Court failed to consider that the defendant did not specifically deny about the death of Ahladi Bewa in their written statement hence the same will be taken to be admitted under Order VIII, rule 3 and 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submissions learned advocate cited decisions reported in 20 DLR 3, 45 DLR 349 and 11 BLT (AD) 139. 25. On the other hand, Mr AKM Badrudduza, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 -opposite parties herein submits that the Appellate Court on proper consideration and elaborate discussion and perusal of the evidence and materials on record rightly set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. He further submits that the trial court clearly found that the plaintiffs did not file the original deed dated 28-4-1952 and 10-5-1969 and they did not state any reasons for not filing the original deed dated 10-5-1969. Though in the plaint they have stated that Madhushudon and Bipod Ranjan executed saf-kabala in favour of the plaintiffs on.13-5-1969 and registered the same in favour of the plaintiffs on 10-5-1969. The Appellate Court observed that deed has been registered before the date of execution. He next submits that the Appellate Court categorically pointed out that the plaintiffs in the suit prayed for cancellation of deed No. 9400 of the defendant dated 21-4-1985 but the plaintiff failed to prove the same by adducing any witness regarding deed that the same was not executed on that date. He also submits that the Appellant Court on careful examination of (Exhibit-5 series) found that the plaintiffs obtained the decree against defendants of present title suit as they were not made party in Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 and the said suit was decreed on ex-parte and further the schedule of the aforesaid two suits are not same. He further submits that the Appellate Court in the judgment clearly found that the plaintiffs claimed the suit land through oral bainanama but in the certified copy of the deed dated 10-5-1969 there was no mention of oral bainanama or contract and none of the PWs made any statement about the oral contract or bainanama in their deposition. He finally submits that the Appellate Court rightly found and came to the conclusion that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession by oral and documentary evidence as such the learned Advocate prayed for discharge of the rule. Learned Advocate again submits that the trial court erroneously passed the decree although the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove their case that Ahladi Bewa died before liberation war and she was not alive at the time of execution and registration of the sub-kabala dated 21-4-1985. 26. Heard the learned Advocate of both the parties, perused the judgment of both the courts below and examined the evidence and materials on record. 27. In the present revisional application since the contending parties are raising claim and counter claim as to the title and possession between the parties. Now core issue which is to be determined in this case is whether the original owner Ahladi Bewa died before liberation war of Bangladesh or after and she was alive at the time of execution and registration of suf-kabala dated 21-4-1985 in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and whether Ahladi Bewa had a son namely Shamboo Nath. 28. Both the parties adduced oral and documentary evidence to prove their respective cases. In this suit plaintiffs to prove their case produced PW 1 Md Iman Uddin, in examination-in-chief he stated that Ahladi Bewa died leaving only son Shambhuo Nath who died leaving wife Sreemoti Bewa, Sreemoti Bewa transferred the suit land to Khetra Mohan Baroi by registered sale deed dated 28-4-1952 (Exhibit-3), that Khetra Mohan Baroi entered into an agreement with the plaintiffs to sell the suit land on 14-10-1961, prior to the registration of the kabala Khetra Mohan died leaving his two sons namely, Modhu Sudhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjon Baroi upon majority they sold away by registered sale deed on 13-5-1969 the land as to which their father entered into a contract to sell to the plaintiffs. He further stated that the original kabala could not file since it has been lost. So he filed certified copy of the kabala dated 13-5-1969 and same was marked as (Exhibit-4). PW 1 further stated that after obtaining the certified copy of the judgment of the Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 passed by the sixth Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka same was decreed ex-parte. After obtaining certified copy of the judgment and decree, he went to Tohsil Office and found that the SA record stands in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Thereafter, he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1990 for correction of record of rights stands in the name of defendants. Accordingly record was corrected. He also denied that since Ahladi Bewa had no son plaintiffs could not file any paper. PW 3 Modhu Sudhan Baroi son of Khetra Mohan Baroi stated in chief that they owned and possessed the suit land by purchasing from Sreemoti Bewa wife of Shamboo Nath son of Iswar Mali and Ahladi Bewa wife of Iswar Mali. He further stated that they sold the suit land to the present plaintiffs in 1969 and since purchase the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. He also asserted that at the time of purchase of the land by his father, Ahladi Bewa was dead. In his cross-examination he stated that it is not a fact that Ahladi Bewa sold the suit land to Sadhu Charan Mondol in 1953. He also denied the suggestion that Ahladi Bewa was alive till 1990 and the record of rights was correctly prepared in her name and during her life time she sold the property in 1985 and delivered possession to defendant Nos. 1 and 2. He also denied the suggestion that Ahladi Bewa was a women of without any issue. The execution of kabala is admitted by him. 29. PW 4 Benu Chowdhury known as Anil Chandra Chowdhury aged 65 years stated in his deposition that the plaintiffs possess the suit land for last 30/32 years by purchasing from Khetra Mohan Baroi and Khetra Mohan Baroi purchased the suit land from wife of Shamboo Nath son of Iswar Mali. He knew Ahladi Bewa, mother of Shamboo Nath who died in the year 1949. The house of Ahladi Bewa and his own house stand beside. In his cross-examination he denied the suggestion that Ahladi Bewa was issueless and Shamboo Nath is not son of Ahladi Bewa and Sreemoti Bewa is not wife of Shamboo Nath. He also denied that Ahladi Bewa was alive till 1990. 30. On the other hand, defendants examined 5 witnesses in this case. Defendant No-1, Ali Akbar deposed in the case on behalf of the defendants, to prove their case in respect of death of the Ahiadi Bewa. DW 1 in support their case stated that they purchased the suit land from Ahiadi Bewa by registered kabala No. 9400 dated 21-4-1985. He further stated that he also purchased the land from Keshob Lal by the said kabala and after purchase he got possession the suit land. In his deposition he stated that “আহলাদি বেওয়া ও কেশব লাল সম্পর্কে শ্যামপুর ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ সার্টিফিকেট দিয়েছে ৮-৫-১৯৮৫ ইং তারিখে। আমি উহা আদালতে দাখিল করিলাম। যাহা প্রদর্শনী-ছ হিসাবে আপত্তি চিহ্নিত হইল।” Defendants to prove their case also produced one Makhon Lal DW 2, who is witness of the defendant's kabala dated 21-4-1985. In chief he stated that the defendants purchased the suit land in 1985. He further stated that he was present at the time of execution of the deed and was a witness of the deed. Ahiadi Bewa was his cousin who died before 7/8 years ago in the year 1991. In his cross examination he stated that it is not true that Ahladi Bewa died in the year 1991. He also stated that Ahiadi Bewa died at the age of 80/85 years. He denied the suggestion that he does not live at Dhania and that he is associated with activities of forgery. 31. DW 3, Modan Lal son of late Keshob Lal stated that in his chief that he neither knew the plaintiffs nor the defendant Ali Akbar and Shamsuddin and his father Keshob Lal sold the suit land to Ali Akbar and Shamsuddin and possession of the transferred land was delivered to them. In his cross-examination he stated that name of his father is Keshob Lal but he has no paper to show that he is son of Keshob Lal. 32. DW 4 Anil Chandra Banik stated in his chief stated that he knows Ahiadi Bewa from 1961 at the time there was a camp and he resides in Dhania area. he said that Ahiadi Bewa had no issue. Suit land was under possession of Ali Akbar and other and he last met with Ahladi Bewa in the year 1985. 33. DW 5 Aminur Islam son of Late Abdul Rahman stated in his chief that the defendants purchased the suit land in 1985 from Ahiadi Bewa and Keshob Lal and he was present at the time of purchase. Ahladi Bewa executed the deed by putting Left Thumb Impression and Keshob Lal by putting signature. He identified Ahiadi Bewa one of the vendors of the kabala. In cross-examination he stated that he lives at Dhaina but there is no holding number in his name. His name also does not appear in the voter list of the area, he had no NID card to show that he is Aminur Islam. He does not know Aminur Islam son of Kudrat Ali appearing in the deed of the defendants. He also denied the suggestion that he has given deposition by false personation of Aminur Islam in exchange of money. 34. We have carefully perused the deposition of the witnesses of both the parties. Let us now consider the evidence led by both the parties on the point of possession. In this connection P.Ws. to prove their possession in the suit land which was corroborated by PWs 2, 3, 5 and 6. Golam Hossain, PW 2 in his deposition stated that he knows the suit land because of her mother has land beside the suit land which is being cultivated by him. To prove possession of the plaintiffs PW 1 produced the certified copy of the kabala executed on 13-5-1969 and registered on 19-5-1969 which was marked as (Exhibit-4). He also filed Exhibit-5 series that is certified copy of the judgment and decree dated 27-3-1989 passed in Title Suit No. 101 of 1986, order of the Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1990 passed by the Assistant Commissioner Land on 24-2-1991 and inquiry held by the Assistant Commissioner Land, Tejgaon Circle and Chairman Shampur Union Parishad submitted report on 10-2-1991 (Exhibit-7) able to prove that the Ahladi Bewa died long before liberation of Bangladesh. He also submitted certified copy of the sole deed which was marked as (Exhibit-9). The learned trial court upon considering the oral and documentary evidence specially Exhibits-4,5,6 and 10 clearly found that the plaintiffs were able to prove their title and possession in the suit land. 35. On the other hand, defendants main case is that Ahladi Bewa died after 1985 and to prove this fact DW 2, Makhon Lal stated in his chief that Ahladi Bewa was his cousin, who died 7/8 years back. In cross-examination he stated she died approximately in the year 1991. DW 4 deposed that Ahladi Bewa was known to him and he met on last time in year 1985. Defendant failed to prove by any documentary evidence that Ahladi Bewa died in 1990/1991 excepting the certificate dated 8-5-1985 (Exhibit-V) issued by Shampur Union Parishad and same was supported by, Md. Ali Akbar defendant no 1 only. Learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite-parties strenuously submits that the defendants were able to prove by evidence that Ahladi Bewa died after liberation of Bangladesh. But this was supported only defendant No.2, who is not a credible witness, though in chief he stated that Ahladi Bewa remain alive since 1990. 36. Let us now examine whether the findings and decisions given by the appellate court which reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff are based on proper consideration of evidence and materials on record. The appellate court in reversing judgment find that the properties of the two suits schedule are not same and as such held that it could not be said that a decree of Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 did not mean it has been passed against the defendants of Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. We have perused the schedule of Title Suit No. 101 of 1986 and schedule 'ka' of the present Title Suit No. 3 of 1991. It appears that the schedule of both the suit are exactly same. 37. That the appellate court further found that the trial court totally overlooked this vital aspect of the case that the plaintiff did not file original deed dated 13-5-1969 and failed to assign any reason for not filing the original deed at the time of filing of the present suit. Moreover, in paragraph No. 3 of the plaint it is stated that Madhu Sudhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjan Baroi executed saf-kabala dated 13-5-1969 and registered the same on 10-5-1959 in this respect the appellate court found that the deed was registered before its execution but appellate court completely overlooking and in not considering the suf-kabala (Exhibit-4) same was executed on 13-5-1969 and registered on 18-5-1969. In this respect PW 1 in his deposition categorically stated that they purchased the suit property from Madhu Sadhan Baroi and Bipod Ranjan Baroi sons of Late Khetra Mohan Baroi by the sale deed which was executed on 13-5-1969 and registered on 19-5-1969(Exhibit-4). The defendants purchased the suit land by the kabala dated 21-4-1985( Exhibit-ga) and (Exhibit-9) and in the said kabala it was stated that the possession of the land was delivered to the vendee-defendants on 1-10-1975 at the time of executing Bainanama. The Vendor, Ahladi Bewa executed the said kabala by putting her LTI and one Aminur Islam identify Ahladi Bewa in the saf-kabala. In the kabala DW 1 and 2 were the attesting witness but none of them in their deposition stated that Ahladi Bewa put her LTI in their presence. Moreover, in examination in chief DW 1 categorically stated that “আমি সম্পত্তি খরিদেও পর দখল পাইয়াছি।” but in the kabala (Exhibit-ga) it is stated that the vendor-Ahladi Bewa delivered possession to the purchaser defendants which is apparently contradictory. But the appellate court totally failed to consider such vital aspect of this case and erroneously set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 38. The positive case of the defendant is that Ahaladi Bewa died not before liberation war but after liberation in the year 1991 but excepting the certificate issued by the Shampur Union Parisad Chairman (Exhibit-V1) defendant failed to produced any reliable dc cuments, such as voter list or any ration card to prove that Ahladi Bewa died after liberation. On the contrary, the plaintiff by Exhibiting 5 (series) and Exhibit-6 successfully proved that Ahladi Bewa died long before liberation war of Bangladesh. It transpires that the plaintiff's kabala is dated 13-5-1959 (Exhibit-4) and defendants kabala was executed on 21-4-1985 (Exhibit-ga) and (Exhibit-9). Since the plaintiffs kabala being the earlier date and plaintiffs are in possession in the suit land for last 30/32 years but the appellate court failed to appreciate such important aspect of this case and erroneously dismissed the suit. 39. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties by referring (Exhibit-cha) submits that Miscellaneous Case No. 275 of 1990 filed by the plaintiffs and by order dated 29-3-1993 stayed the proceeding of miscellaneous case till disposal of the present Title Suit No. 3 of 1991 pending in the third Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka. But there is no scope for the plaintiff to file an application in the miscellaneous case to stay their present title suit but it is evident from the order dated 24-2-1991(Exhibit-6 series) that AC (Land) Tejgaon circle allowed the said Miscellaneous case. It further appears that the appellate court as well as the trial court rightly did not consider this aspect of the case. Rather it appears from Exhibits-7 and 8 that in the said miscellaneous case Assistant Commissioner inquired the matter though the Chairman Shampur Union Parisad. Accordingly Chairman Shampur Union Parisad submitted inquiry report (Exhibit-7) to the Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgoan Circle and the Chairman Shampur Union Parishad issued certificate dated 22-12-1985(Exhibit-8) stating that Ahladi Bewa had died long before the independence. Exhibit-7 speaks that Ahladi Bewa died leaving only son Shamboo Nath and Shamboo Nath died leaving widow Sreemoti Bewa and on the basis of the survey report conducted by the surveyor in miscellaneous case which was filed by the plaintiff for correction of record of right. Accordingly Assistant Commissioner (Land) Tejgaon corrected the record of right and cancelled the record of right published in the name of the defendants by order dated 24-2-1991 (Exhibit-6 series). 40. Thus it appears that the trial court upon consideration of Exhibits-4-6 series rightly passed the decree but appellate court without reversing those findings of the trial court erroneously dismissed the suit. It is the duty of the appellate court to decide the appeal on proper consideration of the evidence as whole. But in the present case appellate court reversed the judgment of the trial court without considering the oral and documentary evidence specially (Exhibits 4-6). Thus the impugned judgment is not passed in accordance with the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this respect reference may be made in the case reported in 11 BLT (AD)139 = 8 BLC (AD) 77 it has been held that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial court. Specially, in the case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. 41. In the present case we find that the specific findings of the trail court have not been reversed by the lower appellate court exercising its power under order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 42. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the decision cited above, we are of the opinion that the learned appellate court committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 43. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 29-8-1999 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Third Court Dhaka in Title Suit No 3 of 1991 is restored and the suit is decreed. The judgment and decree dated 11-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 623 of 1999 are set aside. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby confirmed. Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously. End.
